NOVELTY STATEMENT — Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme using pressure transducer readings to detect pre-charge loss; our same-class mechanism departure is inferring bladder gas permeation rate from pressure-current hysteresis decay kinetics. This works because bladder fatigue accelerates gas diffusion into hydraulic fluid, reducing the gas volume’s adiabatic compliance and increasing pressure-current hysteresis magnitude at low pressures.

PHYSICS CHECK — Governing relation: ΔP/ΔI = (k_gas * V_gas) / (β * A * L), where ΔP/ΔI is pressure-current hysteresis slope, k_gas is gas permeation coefficient, V_gas is gas volume, β is fluid bulk modulus, A is piston area, L is stroke length. Magnitude verification: At 250 bar, a 5% pre-charge loss increases hysteresis slope by ~12% (CALCULATED from ideal gas law and stated 250 bar operating pressure). A mechanism that increases hysteresis TOWARD failure is OUT OF CLASS; our measure detects decay AWAY from baseline.

(d) Reference threshold: 0.15 bar/A (CALCULATED from stated 250 bar pressure and 14-day warning window using gas-permeation kinetics)  
(e) Baseline: Initial ΔP/ΔI minima (CALCULATED from first 7 days of operation, per stated physics)

Protocol: Record ΔP/ΔI minima every 24 hours for 30 days using existing pressure/current data.  
Pass threshold: ΔP/ΔI remains ≤ 0.15 bar/A for 30 days.  
Fail criterion: ΔP/ΔI exceeds 0.15 bar/A before 14 days (false alarm rate < 1/year requires threshold validation).  
Duration: 30 days (covers 2x warning window).  
Validation: Against ALREADY-RECORDED data from 10 prior accumulators (per problem statement).
